readerA.quote: We observe superconducting critical temperatures of Tc = 0.81 K for YRu3B2 and Tc = 0.95 K for LuRu3B2, confirmed through magnetization, specific heat, and electrical transport measurements. [...] A sharp jump was observed in the H = 0 specific heat at Tc = 0.81 K and 0.95 K, respectively, for YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2.
readerA.page_table_or_figure: Full text read from arXiv:2512.16945v2, published as Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023308 (2026). Abstract p.1; superconducting fraction about 100% and magnetization onset 0.70 K on p.2 (Fig. 2); specific-heat Tc on p.3 (Fig. 4); Table I on p.4 (Tc 0.81 K); zero resistance near 0.84 K on p.5 (Fig. 5).
readerA.phase_or_sample: Hexagonal CeCo3B2-type, P6/mmm (a = 5.475 A, c = 3.027 A), Ru kagome net; polycrystalline arc-melted ingot; XRD says phase pure apart from a minute elemental-Ru peak (pattern shown for the Lu analogue).
readerA.tc_criterion: The paper's Tc is the zero-field specific-heat jump (Table I). Magnetization onset at 5 Oe is 0.70 K and zero resistance is near 0.84 K.
readerA.measurement_method: DC magnetization (MPMS with He-3, demagnetization corrected), specific heat (PPMS with dilution refrigerator, down to 60 mK), electrical resistivity (50 mK to 300 K)
readerA.synthesis_conditions: Stoichiometric 1:3:2 mix of Y, Ru and B (each 99.99%), arc-melted on a water-cooled Cu hearth under Ar and remelted several times; mass loss negligible.
readerA.evidence_note: Bulk superconductivity in stoichiometric YRu3B2 at ambient pressure: about 100% shielding plus a specific-heat jump at 0.81 K. Two other groups also report Tc for the same composition: Gaggl et al., Phys. Scr. 101, 055912 (DOI 10.1088/1402-4896/ae3c65, arXiv:2512.09314; Tc about 0.7 K, specific-heat Tc 0.71 K, about 100% shielding; it also notes the older null stopped at 1.2 K), and Winiarski et al., J. Phys. Mater. 9, 025013 (DOI 10.1088/2515-7639/ae6a72, arXiv:2512.08514; Tc = 0.63 K). I read all three full texts on arXiv. All DOIs are registered with Crossref.

readerA.quote: We observe superconducting critical temperatures of Tc = 0.81 K for YRu3B2 and Tc = 0.95 K for LuRu3B2, confirmed through magnetization, specific heat, and electrical transport measurements. [...] The resulting superconducting fraction is close to 100% and 90% respectively in YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2, confirming the bulk superconducting state in both compounds. [...] A sharp jump was observed in the H = 0 specific heat at Tc = 0.81 K and 0.95 K, respectively, for YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2.
readerA.page_table_or_figure: Full text read from arXiv:2512.16945v2 (= Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023308). Abstract p.1; Fig. 1 XRD and about 90% fraction with magnetization onset 0.93 K on p.2 (Fig. 2); specific-heat Tc on p.3 (Fig. 4b,d); Table I on p.4 (Tc 0.95 K); zero resistance near 1.04 K on p.5 (Fig. 5b).
readerA.phase_or_sample: Hexagonal CeCo3B2-type, P6/mmm (a = 5.448 A, c = 3.014 A); polycrystalline arc-melted ingot; XRD shows only a minute elemental-Ru impurity peak (Fig. 1).
readerA.tc_criterion: The paper's Tc is the zero-field specific-heat jump (Table I). Magnetization onset at 5 Oe is 0.93 K and zero resistance is near 1.04 K.
readerA.measurement_method: DC magnetization (MPMS with He-3), specific heat (PPMS with dilution refrigerator, down to 60 mK), electrical resistivity (50 mK to 300 K)
readerA.synthesis_conditions: Stoichiometric 1:3:2 mix of Lu, Ru and B (each 99.99%), arc-melted under Ar on a water-cooled Cu hearth and remelted several times; mass loss negligible.
readerA.evidence_note: Stoichiometric LuRu3B2 is a bulk superconductor at ambient pressure: about 90% shielding fraction and a specific-heat jump at 0.95 K. Only one group reports it, and I found no independent confirmation.

readerA.quote: All measurements confirm the bulk superconducting in ScS with a transition temperature of TC = 5.1(5) K. [...] it exhibits a diamagnetic signal at a superconducting transition temperature of TC,onset = 5.10(5) K, where the electrical resistivity data also shows a zero drop in resistivity [...] Specific heat measurements at zero-field confirmed bulk superconductivity by exhibiting a jump at TC = 4.8(1) K
readerA.page_table_or_figure: Full text read from arXiv:2203.16458v1 (= Phys. Rev. B 106, L020504, 2022). Abstract p.1; Fig. 1(b) magnetization and resistivity and Fig. 1(c) specific heat, with text on p.2; Supplementary Information sec. a (synthesis), Table S1 (structure), Fig. S1 (resistivity onset 5.1(2) K).
readerA.phase_or_sample: Cubic rocksalt (NaCl-type) ScS, Fm-3m, a = 5.172(3) A; polycrystalline arc-melted ingot, single phase by Rietveld refinement within XRD detection limit.
readerA.tc_criterion: The paper's Tc of 5.1 K is the onset of diamagnetism (ZFCW, 1 mT), which coincides with the resistive transition (onset 5.1(2) K). The zero-field specific-heat jump is at 4.8(1) K.
readerA.measurement_method: DC magnetization (SQUID MPMS3, ZFCW/FCC), resistivity and specific heat (PPMS), transverse- and zero-field muon spin rotation (ISIS MuSR, down to 0.3 K)
readerA.synthesis_conditions: Sc ingot and S powder weighed in a 1:1.2 ratio, melted together on a water-cooled Cu hearth under Ar, then flipped and remelted several times.
readerA.evidence_note: Rocksalt ScS is a bulk superconductor at ambient pressure, with about 100% Meissner fraction and a specific-heat jump. Caveats: the paper names the compound ScS but never chemically analyses the product, the starting mix was sulfur-rich (1:1.2), and the 1974 report (Moodenbaugh et al., DOI 10.1016/0025-5408(74)90160-3, abstract not available) is titled 'ScS1+x'. Under a stricter reading of the 0.15 at.% rule this row is weaker than YRu3B2.

readerA.quote: We discover superconductivity in cubic W3Re2C with chiral structure and the superconducting transition temperature Tc is about 6.2 K. [...] it is found that the purest sample can be obtained with the x = 0.8 [...] The EDX analysis for x = 0.8 sample yields the atomic ratio of W to Re is 3 : 1.92(1) when setting W as 3 [...] thus there might also be some Re and C deficiencies in W3Re2C.
readerA.reason_if_not: The composition is not within 0.15 at.%. The paper reports the beta-Mn W3Re2C phase as a bulk superconductor, but the measured sample was made with the nominal ratio W:Re:C = 3:2:0.8, which is about 13.8 at.% C against 16.7 at.% for W3Re2C (2.9 at.% off). EDX gives W:Re = 3:1.92(1), about 0.9 at.% Re-deficient, and the authors say Re and C deficiencies are possible. Samples with nominal x up to 1 are said to have similar Tc (Fig. S5), but those values sit only in the Supporting Information, which I could not reach (pubs.acs.org is blocked here), and those samples contain W2C impurity. If the owner accepts the phase name as the composition, this row would pass every other test: bulk, ambient pressure, Tc 6.2 K.
readerA.page_table_or_figure: Full text read from arXiv:2509.15078v2 (= J. Am. Chem. Soc. 148, 2429-2436, 2026, same authors and title). Abstract p.1; sample composition and EDX on p.6; resistive Tc 6.23 K on p.7 (Fig. 1c); magnetization onset 6.12 K and about 100% shielding at 1.8 K on p.8 (Fig. 1d); specific-heat jump at 6.17 K on p.10 (Fig. 3a).
readerA.phase_or_sample: Cubic beta-Mn-type, P4132 (chiral, noncentrosymmetric), a = 0.68860(2) nm; arc-melted polycrystal of nominal W3Re2C0.8 with a small unreacted-carbon impurity peak.
readerA.tc_criterion: The paper says Tc is 'about 6.2 K' (resistivity drop at 6.23 K). Magnetization onset is 6.12 K and the zero-field specific-heat jump is at 6.17 K.
readerA.measurement_method: Resistivity (PPMS, 2-300 K, up to 9 T), DC magnetization (MPMS3, ZFC/FC at 1 mT, M(H) loops at 1.8 K), specific heat (PPMS)
readerA.synthesis_conditions: W, Re and C powders (99.9%) mixed at W:Re:C = 3:2:x (purest phase at x = 0.8), pressed, arc-melted under ultra-high-purity Ar with a Zr getter, remelted 5-6 times; mass loss under 1%.
readerA.evidence_note: The beta-Mn phase called W3Re2C is a bulk 6.2 K superconductor (about 100% shielding, specific-heat jump), so a label of 0 is probably wrong for the phase. Under the 0.15 at.% rule, however, the measured sample is carbon-deficient (nominal C0.8) and slightly Re-poor by EDX. The owner should decide whether to accept it.

readerA.quote: Title: 'Neutron diffraction and observation of superconductivity for tungsten borides, WB and W2B4'. The only abstract text available (ChemInform, DOI 10.1002/chin.201313007) reads: 'The title compounds are investigated by neutron diffraction and magnetic measurements.'
readerA.reason_if_not: I could not read the paper itself. It is not open access, the FastTrack record has no abstract, and publisher hosts are blocked in this session. I saw no Tc value, sample composition, polymorph or bulk-fraction statement, so nothing can be confirmed from the paper's own text. The reported 4.3 K (tetragonal) and 2.8 K (orthorhombic) values come from the repo notes, not from my reading.
readerA.phase_or_sample: Unknown from the available text (the title names WB and W2B4).
readerA.measurement_method: Neutron diffraction and magnetic measurements (per the ChemInform abstract)
readerA.evidence_note: The DOI is registered and the title claims superconductivity in WB, but no Tc, criterion or bulk evidence could be read. A second search on arXiv found no open copy.

readerA.quote: Here we report the discovery of bulk superconductivity in orthorhombic NbS (o-NbS). [...] o-NbS crystallizes in a MnP-type structure (Pnma) with lattice parameters a = 6.4450(1) A, b = 3.31770(4) A, and c = 5.8629(1) A. It exhibits type-II superconductivity with a critical temperature (Tc) of 6.0 K. Bulk superconductivity is confirmed by the magnetization and heat capacity measurements. [...] the density of states (DOS) on EF is sensitive to niobium vacancies.
readerA.reason_if_not: Only the abstract was available (paywalled, no arXiv preprint found, publisher hosts blocked). The abstract states bulk superconductivity at 6.0 K in o-NbS, but I could not check the measured sample's composition, and the abstract itself flags Nb-vacancy sensitivity, so the sample could be Nb-deficient. I also could not check the Tc criterion, the lowest temperature measured, or a page, table or figure. The training row also does not say which polymorph it means, and an older study found stoichiometric NbS of unstated structure to be non-superconducting.
readerA.page_table_or_figure: Abstract only (Phys. Rev. B 108, 174517, 2023); no page, table or figure could be checked.
readerA.phase_or_sample: Orthorhombic MnP-type NbS, Pnma (per abstract); sample form not read.
readerA.tc_criterion: The abstract gives Tc = 6.0 K; the criterion is not stated in the abstract.
readerA.evidence_note: Strong lead from the abstract, but it cannot meet the two-reader rule without the full text: the composition and Nb vacancies need checking against the paper's body.

readerA.quote: In case of vanadium, κes > κls for T ≥ 2 K. However, the κls of the x = 0.1 alloy starts to increase when the temperature is reduced below TC = 6.4 K
readerA.reason_if_not: No measurement at 12 at.% Ti, and no bracketing series. The only V-Ti series I could read (arXiv:1810.02083) measured x = 0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 and 0.6 (Fig. 1a), plus x = 0.7 'not shown'. The nearest sample above 12 at.% Ti is 30 at.%, far beyond the 2 at.% window; on the low side x = 0.1 sits exactly 2 at.% away. The published version (Paul et al., J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 31, 475801, 2019, DOI 10.1088/1361-648x/ab3515) was available only as an abstract because iopscience is blocked. Other OA V-Ti papers I found study x = 0.35-0.7 or thin films.
readerA.page_table_or_figure: arXiv:1810.02083v1, Fig. 1(a)-(c) (composition list and Tc versus x) on p.4; Tc = 6.4 K for x = 0.1 in the text on p.6.
readerA.phase_or_sample: Body-centred cubic beta-V1-xTix, polycrystalline, arc-melted; x = 0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.6 (and 0.7)
readerA.measurement_method: Resistivity, heat capacity and thermal conductivity (PPMS), 2-8 K for kappa
readerA.synthesis_conditions: Arc melting, characterized by XRD (details in a supplement not included in the arXiv PDF)
readerA.evidence_note: V-Ti alloys on the V-rich side superconduct (6.4 K at 10 at.% Ti), so 12 at.% Ti very likely does too. But no readable paper measures within 0.15 at.% of 12 at.% Ti, and none brackets it within 2 at.% on both sides. arXiv DOIs are registered with DataCite, not Crossref, so a Crossref miss is expected.

I also read two independent full texts that agree: Gaggl et al., Phys. Scr. 101, 055912 (10.1088/1402-4896/ae3c65; Tc 0.71 K from Cp, 0.73 K from magnetization, ~100% shielding) and Winiarski et al., arXiv:2512.08514 (Tc 0.63 K from Cp).

(1) Composition: the paper weighed out the exact 1:3:2 ratio and reports negligible mass loss, so the sample sits on the table composition. (2) Bulk and phase: about 100% demagnetization-corrected shielding plus a specific-heat jump (dCe/gamma Tc about 1.1) rule out a filamentary signal. The only impurity is a minute peak of elemental Ru. Ru's own Tc (about 0.5 K, from general knowledge, not this paper) is below 0.81 K, so it cannot cause the transition. (3) Ambient-pressure polycrystal, not a film. (4) The DOI is registered with Crossref, and its title and 12 authors match the arXiv paper. (5) Tc is stated in Table I. Field check: both readers give the same Tc (0.81 K), criterion, floor (0.05 K), lattice parameters and synthesis. Reader A put Fig. 2 on p.2; it is on p.3 (corrected above). Two independent groups reproduce superconductivity at 0.63 to 0.73 K, depending on the criterion.

verified.verifier_reason: Both readers confirmed, and every test passes except composition: bulk (about 100% Meissner fraction, Cp jump), ambient pressure, single-phase XRD, Tc stated, DOI matching title and authors. On composition I am overruling them, for four reasons. (1) The paper's only composition number is the Sc:S = 1:1.2 weigh-in, with no mass loss, no analysis and no occupancies. (2) The paper calls the structure 'NaCl defect'. (3) The 1974 discovery paper is titled 'Super conductivity in two NaCl structure compounds: alpha-ZrP and ScS1+x' (10.1016/0025-5408(74)90160-3, Crossref/OpenAlex record, not open access). (4) The repo's vendored SuperCon copy (Stanev 2018) lists S1.005Sc1 at Tc = 5.37 K but S1Sc1 at 0. That suggests Tc depends on S/Sc right at stoichiometry, which is exactly what the 0.15 at.% rule tests. The S1Sc1 zero could be a real null at x = 0 rather than a placeholder; I cannot tell without the 1974 paper or Moodenbaugh et al., J. Low Temp. Phys. 33, 175 (1978) (10.1007/bf00117075). Springer and Elsevier are blocked here and neither paper is open access. I treated this the same way as W3Re2C: an off-ratio nominal composition with no analysis fails. This is the owner's call: if the formula the paper names is accepted as the composition (reading the sulfur excess as an allowance for sulfur lost during arc melting), the row passes every other check with tc_k = 5.1.

The readers disagreed, and the paper's own text refutes the exact-composition condition: the sample was nominally C0.8 and EDX measures W:Re = 3:1.92(1), about 1 at.% Re-poor even before the C deficit.
